properties.name: A hub, or any set of designs the person may read, is opened ON DEMAND as one view — N open stores read through one key space namespaced by graph_id — over which every ordinary reflow2 tool runs unchanged; a write through the view lands in the design that owns the node; releasing the view changes nothing, because nothing was copied
properties.statement:
reflow2 SHALL serve a VIEW over N designs held in one process: an agent names a set of graph_ids (a hub's members, or any set the host says the caller may read) and receives one session whose key space is the union of those designs, each id namespaced by its graph_id, so every ordinary tool (search_design, get_node, detect_gaps, propagate_change, seam_coverage, what_next, loop_status, the review relations) runs over the view with no new tool and every id in every reply names its owning design. The view is NOT a copy: it reads the open stores directly, so it cannot go stale and there is nothing to merge back; releasing it costs nothing. A WRITE made through the view lands in the design that owns the node it changes, under that design's single-writer lock; an edge between nodes of two designs is recorded in the design that makes it, as dec:idea-a-relation-between-nodes-in-two-designs-is-recorded-so-linking-works-on-the-one-design settled, never in a third place. PERMISSION IS PER WRITE AS WELL AS PER READ: the host passes the readable set and the writable set; a write into a design the caller may only read is refused naming that design; a design outside the readable set is absent from the view and the view says it is absent without saying what it held. Memoised per-design derived scans (gaps, defects) are COMPOSED from per-design results, as compose_and_analyse already does, not recomputed over the union. CONSEQUENCE FOR HUBS: a hub holds membership and the view, never a copy of a member, which retires the stale-copy problem (a suspended watch, external_dependency pins owed) at its root; the hub-side use is integrated-flo's and flo2's, the primitive is reflow2's. Builds on req:every-cross-design-operation-takes-its-other-designs-by-graph-id-under-the-hosts-read-filter (the named operations by graph_id come first and the view reuses their resolver) and on compose_and_analyse's namespacing (req:composed-analysis). Kept as intent by @ajs 2026-10-10 ("let's keep pressing as much as we can"), after the idea was recorded in his words on dec:idea-cross-design-operations-are-a-primitive-layer-served-by-the-registry-by-graph-id. ═══ BUILD PLAN, 2026-10-11 (door settled in dec:how-a-session-opens-a-view-over-several-designs, option a: the hub's address is the view) ═══
SURVEYED, AND WHY NOT A STORE-LEVEL COMPOSITE NOW: every key begins with the design's id ({graph_id}\0{type}\0{id}, edges, both adjacencies, the property index — keys.rs), and the byte store is a six-method trait (KvBackend: get/put/delete/prefix_scan/prefix_delete/commit_batch). A composite backend routing keys by that prefix is the literal form of this requirement and stays the long-run speed path. But each member's backend is owned by its own StorageEngine (read cache, write buffer, savepoints) behind a tokio RwLock in the mcp crate (SharedGraph), the full-text index is a Tantivy sidecar per engine, and RocksDB opens once per process — so a composite would have to reach through N engines' locks from sync core code. Large, and risky in the core. Recorded, not chosen now.
THE BUILD: A FAN-OUT VIEW AT THE TOOL LAYER, which meets every clause above without a copy:
(1) flo2 passes _meta["reflow2/view_graph_ids"] (the hub's members ∩ the caller's readable set) on every call to a hub's own design; the registry marks that call as a view call. No view _meta → today's behaviour, byte-identical.
(2) ROUTED CALLS: if any string argument names a member id as "<graph_id>:<node id>", the call is a member call — the prefix is stripped from every argument, the call runs on that member's service (opened through the #720 RegistryHandle, its own lock, the caller's writes_for carried), and every node id in the reply is prefixed back. Arguments naming two different members are REFUSED: "a write lands in one design; a relation across designs is a typed link record made in one of them — use review_relations with other_design" (dec:idea-a-relation-between-nodes-in-two-designs-is-recorded-so-linking-works-on-the-one-design). Unprefixed ids stay the hub's own.
(3) FAN-OUT READS: a read-only tool (readOnlyHint true — every tool says so since 0.82.0) with no member id runs on the hub and on each member IN TURN, one read guard at a time (never two), and replies {view: [graph_ids], by_design: {"<graph_id>": <that design's reply, ids prefixed>, ...}, unreachable: [...]}. search_design is the one merged reply: hits from every design ranked together by score, each id prefixed. A member the caller may not read is absent and named in `unreachable` without its content.
(4) FAN-OUT WRITES do not exist: a writing tool with no member id writes the hub's own design, as today.
(5) Every reply through the view says it is a view ("view: [...]"), so a chat never mistakes a merged answer for one design's.
(6) NOT IN THE VIEW: export/import, releases and cuts, claims and holds, seat tools — they belong to one design; through the view they act on the hub's own design only, and say so.
(7) Tests on the start_registry harness: hub H with members A, B; routed get_node / write / refusal of a two-design write; fan-out loop_status and detect_gaps grouped by design; search merged and prefixed; a member outside the readable set absent and named; no view _meta → byte-identical to today; A↔B concurrent calls through two hubs do not deadlock.
Sequence: after #720 (resolver) and 1d (the read tools by graph_id); flo2's half (the view _meta, and readable_graph_ids on reads) ships in the same flo2 PR as layer 1b, after a reflow2 cut and the engine upgrade. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019Xbw6PG9mXJiU2Sb421fnq
